conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the supplied evidence does not support the claim that food-grade wax coatings on apples cause cancer, citing safety re-evaluations from regulatory agencies like EFSA and FDA.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:** The supplied evidence does **not** support the claim that food-grade wax coatings on apples cause cancer.

Apples naturally make a protective wax layer; commercial coatings may be added or restored after washing to reduce moisture loss and handling damage. Coatings vary, but common examples include carnauba wax and shellac, so a claim about “wax” should not assume one single chemical or exposure.

The strongest relevant evidence is regulatory scientific review. EFSA’s expert panel re-evaluated carnauba wax (E903), a food glazing agent, and concluded that estimated exposure from authorized uses had adequate margins of safety relative to observed no-adverse-effect levels. That is evidence against a cancer-risk claim at approved dietary uses—not proof that any substance is risk-free at every dose or in every formulation.  
https://efsa.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2903/j.efsa.2012.2880

In the U.S., FDA guidance specifically addresses the safety and labeling of waxed fruits and vegetables, and requires disclosure arrangements for such coatings; federal food-additive rules also require use under good manufacturing practice.  
https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/cpg-sec-562550-safety-and-labeling-waxed-coated-fruits-and-vegetables  
https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-172

**What is missing:** None of the provided results supplies credible human epidemiology, animal carcinogenicity findings, or a regulatory cancer-hazard determination showing that approved apple wax coatings cause cancer. Viral/social-media assertions cited in the search results are therefore not evidence of causation.

This conclusion applies to **food-grade, authorized coatings used as intended**, not to contamination, non-food-grade wax, or unrelated pesticide residues.
